keyVerseText: And as for Ishmael, I have heard thee: Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly ; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun נָשִׂיא (nâsîyʼ) derives from the root נָשָׂא (nâsâʼ), which means to lift up, bear, or carry. This root conveys the idea of being elevated or exalted, both physically and metaphorically. Thus, נָשִׂיא literally signifies 'one who is lifted up'—an exalted individual such as a chief or leader. This root sense enriches the common English glosses like prince or ruler by emphasizing the dignity and honored status inherent in the office.
usageInScripture: The word נָשִׂיא appears 134 times in the Hebrew Bible and is most often translated as 'prince,' occurring 22 times, with other common renderings including 'captain,' 'chief,' and 'ruler.' This consistent translation pattern highlights its primary function as a title for a person of high rank or authority, often a leader of a tribe or nation. The lexical data show it is used not only for human leaders but also metaphorically for natural phenomena like clouds or vapors, reflecting the idea of something elevated or prominent.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding נָשִׂיא as 'one lifted up' enriches our grasp of biblical leadership as divinely ordained exaltation rather than mere human authority. Leaders in Scripture, from tribal heads to princes, bear the responsibility of representing God's order and purposes on earth. This term reminds believers that true leadership is grounded in being elevated by God’s will and calling, pointing ultimately to Christ, the exalted Prince of Peace who leads with humility and power. It challenges Christians to view earthly authority through the lens of God’s sovereignty and to seek leadership that reflects His glory.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 17:20 declares that Ishmael will father twelve princes, emphasizing God’s blessing and promise of a great nation through him. The use of נָשִׂיא here underscores the significance of these descendants as exalted leaders or chiefs, each bearing the honor and responsibility of governance. This word highlights not only their status but also God’s sovereign role in raising up leaders to fulfill His covenantal purposes.
